correctness.rationale: Inserting/deleting the basepoint before the first change of factor gives a bijective length-preserving matching of every mixed nondegenerate simplex. Each pair has a unique regular face; along every alternating gradient path, a descent that can lead to another lower matched cell strictly decreases the number of nonbasepoint entries, hence no closed path. Positive directed distances bound cells at fixed scale; the critical subcomplex is exactly the factor wedge. The same literal inclusion at every scale yields natural integral persistence decomposition and cross-cup zero. A dependency-free checker verified 76 finite parameter instances, 2521 cells, matching involutions, directed incidence acyclicity and mod-two ranks; these finite checks are supplementary, not the proof.

value.rationale: The explicit universal length-compatible CW matching decomposes all filtered homotopy types, integral homology persistence and positive-degree cup product structure of arbitrary finite strict cut-vertex metrics, including asymmetric directed graph metrics. It computes nontrivial multidegree persistence factorwise and yields a structural result not supplied by known ordinary VR wedge or graded magnitude homology formulas.
